info.title: Release Status Log API
info.description:
Query the history of your account's releases, step by step, so you can monitor release status from your own applications.

Each entry in the log is one step event of a release (for example, `created`, `publishing`, `published`, or `failed`). You choose a time window and get every event that happened in it.

>ℹ️ To learn how to query the log, read more than 1000 entries, and monitor releases continuously, see the [Monitoring release status with the Release Status Log API](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/guides/monitoring-release-status-with-the-release-status-log-api) guide.

## Common parameters

| **Parameter name** | **Description** | **Type** |
| --------------- | ----------------- | ----------------- |
| {{an}} | Name of the VTEX account. Case-insensitive. | Query variable. |
| {{startDate}} | Start of the time window, inclusive. RFC 3339 date-time. | Query variable. |
| {{endDate}} | End of the time window, exclusive. RFC 3339 date-time. | Query variable. |

## Limits

| **Limit** | **Value** |
| --------------- | ----------------- |
| Maximum range between `startDate` and `endDate` | 15 days. |
| Oldest allowed `startDate` | 365 days back (history retention window). |
| Maximum entries per response | 1000. |
| Rate limit | 60 requests per minute per account. |
| Query timeout | 5 seconds. |

To cover a period longer than 15 days, split it into several windows of up to 15 days each.

get.description:
Lists the releases of an account, with cursor pagination. Use it to find a release's name and status. The `id` of each release is the `releaseId` returned by the [Get release history](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/api-reference/release-status-log-api#get-/releases/history) endpoint.

To read the next page, send the request again with `after` set to the `endCursor` value of the previous response, until `hasNextPage` is `false`.

## Permissions

Any user or [API key](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/guides/authentication-overview#api-keys) must have at least one of the appropriate [License Manager resources](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/license-manager-resources--3q6ztrC8YynQf6rdc6euk3) to be able to successfully run this request. Otherwise, they will receive a status code `403` error. These are the applicable resources for this endpoint:

| **Product** | **Category** | **Resource** |
| --------------- | ----------------- | ----------------- |
| Releases | Releases | **Visualize Releases** |

There are no applicable [predefined roles](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/predefined-roles--jGDurZKJHvHJS13LnO7Dy) for this resource list. You must [create a custom role](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/roles--7HKK5Uau2H6wxE1rH5oRbc#creating-a-role) and add at least one of the resources above in order to use this endpoint.

To learn more about machine authentication at VTEX, see [Authentication overview](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/guides/authentication-overview#machine-authentication).

>❗ To prevent integrations from having excessive permissions, consider the [best practices for managing API keys](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/best-practices-api-keys--7b6nD1VMHa49aI5brlOvJm) when assigning License Manager roles to integrations.

parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Number of releases to return in the page. Minimum of 1 and maximum of 30. If not informed, the default is 10.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Cursor that indicates where the page starts. Use the `endCursor` value returned in the previous response to get the next page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filters releases by status. To filter by more than one status, separate them with commas, for example, `UNSCHEDULED,PUBLISHING`.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: Sorting criteria, in the format `FIELD,DIRECTION`. The field can be `LAST_MODIFIED` or `START_DATE`, and the direction can be `ASC` or `DESC`. For example, `LAST_MODIFIED,DESC`.

items.description: Object with data of a release.

id.description: Unique identifier of the release. It is the `releaseId` returned by the Get release history endpoint.

description.description: Description of the release. Omitted when it has no value.

lastModified.description: Date and time of the last modification of the release, in RFC 3339 format and UTC. Omitted when it has no value.

lastStatusUpdate.description: Date and time of the last status change of the release, in RFC 3339 format and UTC. Omitted when it has no value.

startDate.description: Date and time when the release is scheduled to be published, in RFC 3339 format and UTC. Omitted when it has no value.

endDate.description: Date and time when the scheduled release ends, in RFC 3339 format and UTC. Omitted when it has no value.

reason.description: Reason for the failure when the release status is `FAILED`. Omitted when it has no value.

service.description: Name of the service that caused the failure.

endCursor.description: Cursor of the last release in the page. Use it as the `after` parameter to get the next page. Omitted when the page is empty.

hasNextPage.description: Indicates whether there are more releases after this page.

totalCount.description: Total number of releases that match the request.

get.description:
Retrieves the log of release step events that happened in a time window, sorted by `occurredAt` in ascending order. The window is `[startDate, endDate)`.

All events of a release share the same `releaseId`. Group entries by it to read the release's sequence, for example: `created > publishing > enqueued > build_succeeded > published`. A step can happen more than once for the same release.

Release names are not included in the log. To find a release's name, use the [List releases](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/api-reference/release-status-log-api#get-/releases) endpoint. Its `id` is the `releaseId` returned here.

A response holds at most 1000 entries. When `truncated` is `true`, more entries exist in the window. To learn how to read them, handle the `429` and `503` status codes, and poll the endpoint continuously, see the [Monitoring release status with the Release Status Log API](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/guides/monitoring-release-status-with-the-release-status-log-api) guide.

## Permissions

Any user or [API key](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/guides/authentication-overview#api-keys) must have at least one of the appropriate [License Manager resources](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/license-manager-resources--3q6ztrC8YynQf6rdc6euk3) to be able to successfully run this request. Otherwise, they will receive a status code `403` error. These are the applicable resources for this endpoint:

| **Product** | **Category** | **Resource** |
| --------------- | ----------------- | ----------------- |
| Releases | Releases | **Visualize Releases** |

The token must also have been issued for the same account informed in the `an` query parameter. A token issued for another account is refused with a `403` status code, even if its user has a role in that account. For an API key, the account is the one the key belongs to.

There are no applicable [predefined roles](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/predefined-roles--jGDurZKJHvHJS13LnO7Dy) for this resource list. You must [create a custom role](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/roles--7HKK5Uau2H6wxE1rH5oRbc#creating-a-role) and add at least one of the resources above in order to use this endpoint.

To learn more about machine authentication at VTEX, see [Authentication overview](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/guides/authentication-overview#machine-authentication).

>❗ To prevent integrations from having excessive permissions, consider the [best practices for managing API keys](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/best-practices-api-keys--7b6nD1VMHa49aI5brlOvJm) when assigning License Manager roles to integrations.

parameters.name: an
parameters.description: Name of the VTEX account. Case-insensitive, so `Acme` and `acme` return the same entries.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Start of the time window, **inclusive**. RFC 3339 date-time. It cannot be older than the history retention window (365 days).

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: End of the time window, **exclusive**. RFC 3339 date-time. It must be after `startDate`, and the range between both dates cannot exceed 15 days. A date in the future is accepted.

history.description: Log entries sorted by `occurredAt` in ascending order. Contains at most 1000 entries per response.

items.description: Object with data of a release step event.

id.description: Unique identifier of the log entry.

releaseId.description: Identifier of the release this event belongs to.

accountName.description: Name of the account that owns the release.

step.description: Step of the release that this event represents.

occurredAt.description: Date and time when the event happened, in RFC 3339 format and UTC.

outcome.description: Outcome of the step. Omitted when it has no value.

reason.description: Free-text reason for the event. Omitted when it has no value.

error.description: Error details when the step failed. Omitted when it has no value.

actor.description: Who or what triggered the event. Omitted when it has no value.

type.description: Type of the actor that triggered the event, for example, `user`.

app.description: Name of the app that triggered the event.

related.description: Objects related to the event. Omitted when it has no value.

truncated.description: Indicates whether more entries exist in the time window than the ones returned. When `true`, repeat the request using `lastOccurredAt` as the new `startDate`.

lastOccurredAt.description: Timestamp of the last returned entry. Omitted when `history` is empty.
